The passage describes how the former kings of Xia initially cultivated virtue and avoided calamities, but their descendant failed to do so, leading Heaven to send down calamities and favor the Shang ruler instead. The phrase “Heaven sent down calamities, using our ruler, who possessed of its favor” indicates that the current ruler (of Shang) had received divine approval to replace the Xia, which aligns with the concept of the Mandate of Heaven in ancient Chinese political thought.
